reviewer_checks_pass: The packet check matched the exact candidate, spec SHA-256, and packet SHA-256.

The schema appends an optional RawPtrKind field to RawPtrData and defines a closed union for Mut, Const, and FakeForPtrMetadata. The exporter fills the discriminator for every real RawPtr and retains the legacy mutability field. Legacy/synthetic records can omit the optional field; the R23 projection rejects absent or null payloads.

The R23 reader rejects every kind except exact Mut, separately requires legacy mutability Mut, and rejects unknown union cases. This preserves the semantic distinction that FakeForPtrMetadata can share a lossy mutable mapping but has different borrow-checker/retag behavior. The Rustc enum documents FakeForPtrMetadata as metadata-only and distinct from Mut: https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_middle/mir/enum.RawPtrKind.html.

Exporter admission permits a RawPtr only as the first value-projection assignment, with RawPtrKind::Mut, receiver local _1, exactly one Deref projection, a non-argument/non-return local destination, and exactly one final PtrToPtr cast from that raw-pointer local into return local _0. Other RawPtr kinds/shapes and extra assignments after this sequence remain unsupported.

Translator independently requires the exact &mut [u64] receiver and *mut [u64] intermediate type, canonical input local, mutable-reference place kind, single Deref, live storage, and non-input/non-return destination. The next cast must consume that exact local, target the output local, be the only cast after the raw-pointer step, have typed raw-mut slice to raw-mut u64 endpoints, and be PtrToPtr. Missing or extra final casts fail.

The operation is represented as its own `raw-ptr-mut-deref` trace step with input/output local ordinals and typed edge; the final pointer cast is a separate trace step. Structural equality compares the full std-cal-lee and helper projection records, including operation kind, typed edges, source order, storage events, local count/order/mutability, and body counts. RawPtr kind or place shape is not erased by normalization.

The original cast-only projection remains available when no RawPtr step occurs: old Use/Cast admission remains limited to the prior linear body constraints. If a RawPtr step occurs, it must be first and can only be followed by the one exact final cast. No load/store, index, nested projection, pointer arithmetic, extra reference, call, branch, or additional projection operation is newly admitted.

P13's complete bounded storage lifecycle remains enforced: all events stay serialized and counted; marked pointer temporaries require one initialized, live, non-overlapping Live/Dead pair; operands and destinations must be live; all other non-assignment statements remain refused. Source marker/lifetime binding, exact caller Ref/Unsize/call chain, verified same-unit helper contract, full_borrow resource restoration, and normal/unwind path checks remain in force.
